contracts: Split pane menu and close controls use RustActionView plain View hosts without Button/ButtonController instances. Metal scene items consume the shared Rust action snapshot; fallback retains the shared glyph painter. Native comparison remains SceneGlyphButton.

Both pane bars revoke pending Rust input when pane View pointers or orientation change. Domain workspace/index/128-bit identity/visibility changes also revoke input; ordinary title/focus updates preserve the target. Native input, focus, accessibility, menu and window adapters remain.
CloseSplitPane deferred callbacks capture an opaque tab identity, resolve its current index at execution, and ignore deleted targets or changed workspaces. This correction applies to both backends.

The shared ownership case checks all four hosts, AX roles/names, geometry, disabled rejection, the real Cocoa menu, physical main-window Space, and Rust late release after swap, orientation, unsplit/replacement and hide/restore. A second case verifies queued close after a lower-index deletion and queued close of an already-deleted target.

Existing native mouse/gesture divider, split orientation/title/fallback/close, split lifecycle/persistence/isolation and control-family regressions retain their semantic assertions. No dependency, store, persistence or browser service policy changed.
